Americas.headline: Venezuela — Consecutive Earthquakes Cause Mass Casualties and Crisis
Americas.body: One week after consecutive magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 earthquakes struck Venezuela, authorities report nearly 3,000 fatalities, with tens of thousands of people still missing. Rescue operations continue under grueling conditions, though officials warn the likelihood of finding additional survivors under the rubble has grown slim. Aerial footage demonstrates catastrophic damage in the hardest-hit urban areas. The disaster has triggered a widening crisis and highlighted systemwide infrastructure failures, severely increasing emergency relief needs across affected communities.

Americas.headline: Haiti — Gang Violence Kills 47 and Displaces Thousands in Capital
Americas.body: Escalating gang violence in the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area continues to inflict severe civilian casualties and drive displacement. The United Nations confirmed an attack in Kenscoff that killed at least 47 people, including five children, and resulted in more than 50 kidnappings. An armed group leader threatened to murder hostages if security forces attempt rescues. Separately, intensified clashes in Croix-des-Bouquets have displaced approximately 2,000 people since mid-October, further restricting access to essential services and deepening the humanitarian crisis.

Africa.headline: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Ebola Outbreak Escalates Amid Insecurity and Food Crisis
Africa.body: Six months into the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak, response efforts remain severely hampered by armed conflict, widespread hunger, and targeted violence. The World Health Organization has verified 81 attacks on health facilities, isolating responders from over 1,000 exposed individuals. Armed groups, including the Allied Democratic Forces, continue attacking civilians across Ituri and North Kivu provinces. Approximately two-thirds of recent deaths have occurred within communities outside treatment centers. Furthermore, an estimated 28.8 million people face severe food insecurity across the country. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, spans 68 health zones across eight provinces.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Energy grid attacks and civilian casualties heighten winter humanitarian risks
Europe.body: Intensified Russian strikes across Ukraine targeting energy and railway infrastructure killed at least three people and threatened essential services ahead of winter. UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator Matthias Schmale warned that targeting power grids severely imperils water supplies, heating, and frontline aid operations, deepening the humanitarian crisis. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky noted that recent Russian attacks were enabled partly by restrictions placed on Ukraine's access to SpaceX's Starshield service.

Europe.headline: Ukraine/Russia — Ukrainian forces target Kerch Strait bridge in major strike escalation
Europe.body: Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Strait bridge connecting Russia to occupied Crimea, restricting traffic across the passage according to local Russian-backed officials. The attack coincided with what Russian defense ministry data indicates is the largest Ukrainian drone operation launched against Russian territory since the beginning of the war.

Europe.headline: Estonia — Border with Russia to close following suspected sabotage attack
Europe.body: Estonia announced plans to close all border crossing points with Russia starting December 1. The decision by Estonian authorities follows an attempted arson attack targeting a domestic drone manufacturer, an action Tallinn attributed to suspected Russian sabotage.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Philippines — Magnitude 7.8 Earthquake Kills at Least 32 in South
Asia-Pacific.body: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck the southern Philippines on Monday, killing at least 32 people and injuring 200 others, according to Philippine civil defense officials. At least 12 people remain missing, with emergency rescue operations underway amid reports that victims may be trapped inside a school building. Authorities reported that initial tsunami warnings have mostly been lifted as damage assessments continue across the affected region.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar — Military Air Strike Kills 12 at Displaced Persons Camp in Rakhine State
Asia-Pacific.body: A Myanmar military air strike on Friday evening struck the Byar La displacement camp in Ponnagyun township, northeast of Sittwe in Rakhine state, killing 12 people. Witnesses and rescue workers reported widespread destruction at the camp, which shelters civilians displaced by Myanmar's ongoing conflict. The attack resulted in multiple civilian casualties, including children and family members of local residents.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Indonesia — Heavy Rainfall Causes Severe Flooding Across West Java
Asia-Pacific.body: Days of heavy rainfall caused the Citoe River to overflow in Cipatujah, West Java province, causing severe flooding in residential areas, farmland, and plantations. Water levels reached approximately one metre in affected locations, including Cipanas village. The rising floodwaters submerged homes, swallowed a local bridge, and blocked major transportation routes, preventing residents from accessing nearby communities.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Indonesia — Warnings Issued for High Waves from Developing Cyclone Systems
Asia-Pacific.body: Indonesia's meteorology agency warned on Monday that two developing tropical cyclone systems near Indonesian waters could generate stronger winds and ocean waves up to four metres high. The systems, identified as Tropical Cyclone Seed 92B in the Bay of Bengal and Seed 96S west of Sumatra, are influencing regional wind patterns and creating risks for coastal residents and maritime workers.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Ebola Outbreak Spreads to 5 Countries, 5,500 Dead
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has now killed 5,568 people and infected 11,376 as of November 14. Cases have also turned up in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria and France. Six months after it was declared, it is the second largest Ebola outbreak in recorded history. Health officials in Congo declared the outbreak on May 15, 2026. Two days later the World Health Organization classified it as a public health emergency of international concern, its highest level of alarm. The virus has since spread across eight Congolese provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, Haut Uele, Tshopo, South Kivu, Bas Uele, South Ubangi and North Ubangi.
